newsitem.title: UK: UK manufacturing demand improves in November - CBI.
newsitem.headline: UK manufacturing demand improves in November - CBI.

text.p: Overall demand for manufactured goods in Britain improved in November, according to the latest Confederation of British Industry (CBI) monthly industrial trends survey.
Twenty-four percent of firms said their present order books were above normal and 24 percent below normal, giving an overall balance of zero, the most positive result since August 1995.
This compares with a negative balance of nine percent in the last two surveys.
Export orders remained weak although the position had improved slightly since last month, despite the strong pound.
"The improvement in demand in November is a good result compared with the previous surveys, but is from a low base," said Sudhir Junankar, CBI associate director of economic analysis.
"Export demand also continues to be relatively sluggish, although the slight improvement this month is surprising given the recent strengthening in sterling."
Junankar said firms were starting to make a dent in their stocks of finished goods, so the recovery in manufacturing output seemed likely to take root.

Manufacturers expect domestic prices to rise over the next four months. Price expectations have risen since September, partly due to seasonal factors, following a downward trend during the first half of this year.

"The pick-up in prices is a warning signal but expectations indicated in this survey are much lower than a year ago and competitive pressures continue to hamper the ability of manufacturers to achieve price rises in their home market," Junankar said.

Firms expect to increase output over the next four months at a similar rate to that of the past two months. The November positive balance of 21 percent confirmed the more positive trend in output expectations apparent since the middle of this year.
Stocks of finished goods remained more than adequate to meet demand but had been run down slightly since October.
